Kyiv opens new river tram line

By Olena Kovalenko, 2 November 2026

The city opened its first river tram line on Monday, linking Poshtova Square with the Obolon embankment in twenty-two minutes, about half the time the same trip takes by road at rush hour.

Eight low-floor trams run every twelve minutes from six in the morning until midnight. Tickets cost the same as on the metro, and the transport card works on board.

Why the river

Planners chose the embankment because the land already belonged to the city, so construction took fourteen months instead of the three years a new street line would have needed, according to the transport department.

“We built on what we had, and we built it fast,” said the head of the department, Andriy Melnyk.

The line has nine stops, four of them with heated shelters for the winter. A second stage to Vyshhorod is planned for 2028, if the budget allows.

What riders said

  • Most people we asked liked the speed and the view.
  • Some complained that the trams are crowded between eight and nine.
  • Cyclists asked for racks on board; the department promised two per car next year.

The full timetable is on the transport department's page.
